full_citation: Baumeister, Huber, Lee & Ravazzolo (2024), Forecasting Natural Gas Prices in Real Time, NBER Working Paper 33156
data: real-time (PIT) database + univariate, VAR/BVAR, energy-price-spread, and forecast-pooling models
target: monthly average real Henry Hub spot price
method: ARMA/AR/BVAR/exponential smoothing/price-spread/regime-switching + Model Confidence Set pooling
validation_method: true real-time recursive out-of-sample evaluation vs random-walk benchmark (1997-2024)
main_result: OOS demonstrated: parsimonious BVAR(1) with 6 fundamentals beats random walk at ALL horizons (14-24% MSPE reduction, growing with horizon); futures-based forecasts beat RW at all horizons; MCS-selected forecast pooling gives the largest gains (up to ~54% MSPE reduction at h=24, real-time selected).
evidence_type: This is a rare genuinely PIT-governed natural-gas forecasting study -- authors built a real-time vintage database explicitly to avoid look-ahead bias; directly usable as a PIT-methodology template.
out_of_sample_evidence: Very high -- explicitly documents 4 distinct historical regimes (pre-2006 oil-linkage; 2006-2009 shale transition; 2010-2016 shut-in fracking / decoupling from oil; 2016-present LNG-export recoupling) and shows the BEST-PERFORMING MODEL CLASS CHANGES BY REGIME
pit_validity: No H-GLOBAL-LNG-1-specific test (US-only fundamentals; no TTF/JKM variables in the model)
structural_regime_relevance: US-only fundamentals model; earlier crude-oil price-spread cointegration model breaks down in Jan 2009 and this break was NOT detectable in real time by a Markov-switching extension -- a cautionary finding for any regime-switching design.
supports_h_global_lng_1: Overparameterised long-lag VARs (VAR(12)) underperform the random walk; parsimony (lag 1) plus stochastic volatility materially outperforms complexity; no single model wins at every horizon -- forecast POOLING is required for best results; oil-gas price-spread cointegration model produced dismal forecasts post-2009 break
candidate_mechanism: None found in this pass -- data, code framework and vintage sources are documented in the paper's own appendix (Table 1A)
limitations: Highest of any single source retrieved -- directly informs Commodity's target/horizon/PIT design and gives a credible
replication_concerns: real-time-validated baseline that beats a zero-return-equivalent naive benchmark
commodity_relevance: retain -- primary methodological anchor for the forecasting-literature review and for target/horizon design criticism
